newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai army plans to move Karen refugees to safety.
newsitem.headline: Thai army plans to move Karen refugees to safety.

text.p: Thailand's army chief said on Friday that he planned to move thousands of displaced Burmese Karen refugees to safer areas way from the Burmese border after recent attacks on them by a rival group.
"I am insisting on my earlier proposal to relocate the refugees camps by moving them away from the border at least 10 km (six miles) deeper inside Thailand," General Chetta Tanarajo told reporters.
He said he would put his plan to the National Security Council (NSC), which is chaired by Prime Minister Chavalit Yonchaiyudh and is responsible for refugee policies, at its next meeting.
About 70,000 ethnic Karen refugees, mostly families of Karen National Union (KNU) guerrillas, have been living in sprawling refugee camps along the border for years.
Several of the camps are located just metres (yards) from the Moie river, which marks the border between Thailand and Burma.
The KNU has been fighting the Rangoon government for greater autonomy for the Karen state since 1948.
Last week, the refugees came under serious attacks from a rival Karen faction, the Democratic Karen Buddhist Army (DKBA), which split from the Christian-dominated KNU in early 1995.
The DKBA, said to be backed by Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC), in its latest attacks on the KNU burnt three refugee camps and killed three people.

"This happened because of the lack of Thai armed forces to take responsibility for our protection," the refugee Karen Students Network Group said in letters to the Thai government and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
The student group appealed to the Thai interior ministry and the UNHCR to take the plight of the Karen refugees more seriously.
